title: Parameter onboarding checklist and hotpatching guidelines
content:
Purpose:
This is a working checklist + operational playbook for bringing new model parameter artifacts into the serving fleet and for performing low-risk parameter hotpatches (minor weight fixes, quantization swaps, bugfix checkpoints). The doc captures the expected lifecycle from artifact ingestion to full residency, the minimal validation steps, a safe hotpatch protocol for live replicas, and KV-cache coordination to avoid stale attention caches.

Scope and assumptions:
- Focus on parameter blobs (safetensors / .pt / quantized shards) that are sharded and served from the runtime via mmap or a memory-backed allocator.
- This is NOT a retraining/change-in-graph procedure. We assume identical model topology; changes that affect kernel shapes require a different rollout.
- Rollouts may target hosted, dedicated, and private deployments; operational controls should be the same but some steps may be manual in private installs.

High-level lifecycle (stages):
1) Ingest – artifact pushed to object store + metadata registered in model-catalog.
2) Preflight validation – checksum, shape/metadata verification, compatibility matrix check against kernel table.
3) Offline quantization & quick eval (optional) – small perf pass to ensure token-level parity within tolerance.
4) Prefetch pass – proactive mmap/preload of high-priority pages on a canary subset.
5) Canary swap – atomic pointer/descriptor swap for a replica group with traffic steering.
6) Observability window – validate traces, latency, token-level divergence, and KV-cache hit behavior.
7) Fleet rollout – gradual widening with automated fallback.

Preflight checklist (artifact producer):
- [ ] SHA256 and CRC32 computed and stored in metadata.
- [ ] safetensors schema version stamped (if safetensors).
- [ ] Per-shard dimension table included and validated.
- [ ] Quantization metadata present: scale vectors, q-type, per-channel flags.
- [ ] Compatibility profile: required kernel capabilities (fp16, int8-avx512, fused-attn-v2).
- [ ] Minimum runtime version required for this artifact.
- [ ] Quick inference smoke test (unit prompts) results attached.

Runtime preflight (automated):
- checksum verification against stored digest.
- verify shard counts and shapes against expected topology.
- verify kernel compatibility table on target hosts; fail early if required ops not present.
- compute residency estimate: memory footprint, working set (estimated hottest pages), and suggested prefetch budget.

Hotpatch protocol (design goals):
- Atomic swap: ensure no request sees a partially applied set of shards.
- Minimal dwell time with new artifact in memory before traffic flows (probe + read-only dry run).
- KV-cache correctness: invalidate only necessary keys/prefixes to avoid full-session resets when safe.
- Fallbackable: if any invariant fails, runtime rolls back to previous descriptor quickly with minimal allocation churn.

Atomic hotpatch sequence (per-replica):
1) Stage new artifact on local temp path (download to /dev/shm or fs with pre-allocated space).
2) Validate on-host checksums and shape; if safetensors then run parser validation.
3) Create mmap descriptor(s) for each shard without publishing to the request path.
4) Warm pages: touch a prioritized subset of pages (embedding + attention key/value projection blocks) according to prefetch scoring.
5) Install sentinel descriptor: publish a new descriptor object in-memory that points to new shards but keeps a ready=true flag = false. Incoming requests are routed to the old descriptor.
6) Dry-run verification: run 1-5 short inference traces through the new descriptor under no-user-traffic flag. Ensure outputs are within tolerance and no kernel faults occur.
7) Flip ready=true atomically (single-atomic-store) so dispatcher sees the new descriptor as live.
8) Start gradual traffic shift for this replica group (canary weight). Monitor metrics; on failure, atomically reset descriptor pointer back to previous object and unmap new shards.

Notes on atomicity and memory safety:
- Descriptor pointer must be a single aligned atomic word readable by all request threads. Use double-buffered descriptor arrays to avoid ABA issues.
- When unmapping old shards, ensure no live threads hold references to mmap pages. Use epoch-based grace period: after pointer swap, wait for max request latency + 2x jitter before unmap.
- Provide a runtime API to pin a descriptor for the duration of a request to avoid races.

KV-cache coordination rules:
- KV cache keys are derived from per-layer key/value content + descriptor-version tag. When descriptor changes in a non-bitwise-identical way, evict affected layer keys:
  - conservative: evict entire session-level cache for sessions that touched modified layers.
  - targeted: if metadata includes page-to-layer map and changed pages are small, issue targeted invalidations for layer id + descriptor hash.
- Implementation: keep (layer_id, descriptor_hash) in cache keys. Hotpatch that changes descriptor_hash automatically causes cache miss which is safe. Consider partial invalidation for bandwidth-sensitive workloads.

Prefetch & eviction prioritization heuristics (proposal):
- Score(page) = alpha * access_frequency + beta * recent_kv_hits + gamma * layer_importance - delta * page_load_cost
- Layer importance: projection matrices that produce KV vectors and first-token embeddings have higher weight.
- Access_frequency and recent_kv_hits are derived from short-term telemetry.
- page_load_cost approximates network/disk latency and decompression time.
- Eviction policy: age-based with decayed-frequency softening to prefer keeping pages that accelerate next-token generation latency.

Kernel affinity and hotpatch interaction:
- When new artifact requires different fused kernels (e.g., fused-attn-v2), validate kernel table and ensure binary artifacts are present before descriptor flip.
- If kernel replacement is required, prefer node-level scheduling drain: cordon node, apply kernel, bootstrap runtime unit tests, then resume canary. Avoid in-place kernel swap during live traffic unless absolutely necessary.

Rollback and failure modes:
- Failure during dry-run: unmap new shards, clear temp files, mark artifact as failed in catalog.
- Failure after flip: immediate rollback via atomic pointer reset, begin rolling unmap after grace epoch, mark incident ticket with trace ids and per-request diffs.
- Undetectable divergence: capture eval prompts and user traces during canary, run offline diff harness. If quality regressions are found, rollback and require artifact producer fixes.

Operational checklist for a canary rollout (engineer runbook):
- Pre: ensure artifact metadata present.
- Step 0: create canary job in rollout controller with target replica set and canary weight 5%.
- Step 1: controller instructs replicas to stage artifact and run dry-run.
- Step 2: controller opens observability window (15m default) with automated alerts: latency p95, p99, error-rate, token-delta threshold, kv-hit ratio drift.
- Step 3: if stable, increase weight to 25% over 30m. Repeat observability.
- Step 4: to 50% then 100% following same cadence.
- Step 5: monitor longer (2h) at 100% before marking rollout as complete.

Testing & validation matrix (minimal):
- unit: safetensors parser, checksum validator, descriptor atomic swap.
- integration: stage & flip on single replica under synthetic load, ensure graceful unmap.
- soak: 24h canary with production traffic replay.
- chaos: simulate OOM during prefetch, disk-read failure during mmap open.

Open questions / action items:
- Q: Do we want descriptor-level semantic versioning separate from artifact hashes? Action: proposal by 2025-10-15.
- Q: Can we provide targeted KV invalidation without adding heavy per-page metadata? Action: prototype targeted invalidation in branch runtime/kv-invalidate.
- Q: Do private deployments require a different package for staged warm pages (tmpfs vs direct-mmap)? Action: ops to document differences.

TODOs:
- [ ] Add exact atomic descriptor memory layout and C++ struct for double-buffered descriptor. (owner: Daniel)
- [ ] Draft the observability alert runbook for token-delta regression. (owner: María)
- [ ] Implement epoch-based pinning API and add unit tests. (owner: Omar)

Notes to self:
- Keep hotpatch logic conservative for first 6 months; prefer node-level drains for any kernel-level requirement.
- Avoid full-session KV evictions unless necessary; drive adoption of descriptor-tagged keys to make evictions automatic.

References & links:
- runtime PR for descriptor API: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/487
- related rollout controller design: confluence:RolloutController-Design
- example Jira for a recent hotpatch: ENG-1429

End of doc - this is an iterative working checklist. Expect addenda as we prototype the descriptor atomic type and targeted KV invalidation primitives.
